findings.summary: The new rule hides the inviter until acceptance, which contradicts the Invitation screen's InvitePreview shown before Accept/Decline and leaves the invitee with no way to know whom they are consenting to connect with.
findings.evidence: Added: "Opening the invitation does not reveal who sent it until it has been accepted" / "the inviter stays anonymous until acceptance"; screen.invitation: "Exactly InvitePreview and ConsentPanel after validation; Accept and Decline controls"

findings.summary: Blind acceptance undermines the feature's "two explicit consents" model, because the invitee's acceptance no longer consents to a known counterpart, and no consent or policy node was updated to say what the invitee is agreeing to.
findings.evidence: GD.connect: "pairs formed by two explicit consents; the inviter stays anonymous until acceptance"; policy.pairConsent: "creating the invitation and accepting it provide the two consents"

findings.summary: The anonymity behaviour is placed on the inviter-side Invite affordance, even though it governs what the invitee sees on screen.invitation, and the new criterion clause is not reflected in that screen or in operation.invite.accept.
findings.evidence: affordance.ConnectionPanel.invite effects: "Opening the invitation does not reveal who sent it until it has been accepted"; screen.invitation and operation.invite.accept are unchanged
